question: If a solid sphere of radius 10 cm is melted into 8 spherical solid balls of equal radius, then what will be the surface area of each such ball ? [Use π = frac{{22}}{7}]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a sphere is melted into 'n' equal smaller spheres, the new radius becomes r = R ÷ n¹/³.

Here, n = 8, so the new radius r = 10 ÷ 8¹/³ = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.

Surface area of each new small ball = 4πr²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × (22/7) × 5² = 2200/7 = 314 2/7 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 314 2/7 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the original solid sphere (R) = 10 cm

Number of identical spherical balls formed (n) = 8

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = 4/3 × π × r³

Surface Area of a sphere = 4 × π × r²

 
 
 
 
• 
 R = 10
 Original Sphere

 
 
• 
 

 Melted into
 8 balls

 
 
 
 
• 
 r = ?
 8 Equal Balls
 
 
 
 
 
 

**Calculations:**

Let the radius of each newly formed small spherical ball be r.

Since the large sphere is melted to form 8 identical balls, the total volume remains conserved.

⇒ Volume of large sphere = 8 × Volume of one small ball

⇒ 4/3 × π × R³ = 8 × (4/3 × π × r³)

⇒ R³ = 8 × r³

⇒ 10³ = 8 × r³

⇒ 1000 = 8r³

⇒ r³ = 1000 ÷ 8

⇒ r³ = 125

⇒ r = 5 cm

⇒ Surface Area of each small ball = 4 × π × r²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × (22/7) × 5²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × (22/7) × 25

⇒ Surface Area = 100 × (22/7)

⇒ Surface Area = 2200/7 cm²

⇒ 2200 ÷ 7 = 314 with a remainder of 2

⇒ Surface Area = 314 2/7 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 314 2/7 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a 3D object is melted and recast into other shapes, the total volume always remains constant, even though the combined surface area changes significantly.

Sphere Formulas

Volume of a Sphere = 4/3 × π × r³
Surface Area of a Sphere = 4 × π × r²

Hemisphere Formulas

Volume of a Hemisphere = 2/3 × π × r³
Curved Surface Area = 2 × π × r²
Total Surface Area = 3 × π × r²
